# Mining laser

## Problem statement

Asteroids are an inert world hazard that drift through the field and drop minerals when destroyed (small asteroids drop one mineral; a large chain is 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 destroys). Mining them competes directly with shooting the actual threats, so mineral farming is a manual detour. Add a **Mining Laser** power-up: a rapid-firing laser that only ever targets asteroids and always fires at the nearest one, so the player can farm minerals passively while keeping their normal weapon trained on enemies.

## Users

- **Player (primary).** Wants minerals for the hold/reward loop without diverting aim from enemies.
- **Game/balance designer.** Wants one clean, data-driven power-up kind with tunable fire rate, damage and duration.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I collect a Mining Laser my ship automatically fires rapid laser shots at the nearest asteroid, so I can farm minerals without stopping my attack on enemies.
- As a player, the Mining Laser never wastes shots on empty space or on enemies — it only fires at a live asteroid.
- As a player, when there are no asteroids, the Mining Laser is silent and does not distract me.

## Resolved decisions (producer answers)

- **D1 — Delivery model.** It is a **normal weapon power-up** that occupies one of the six loadout slots when permanently owned, and it has **upgrade levels** (the standard power-up level curve). It is an additive auxiliary weapon: collecting it does **not** replace the cannon, so the player can still damage enemies.
- **D2 — Acquisition & duration.** It is acquired as a **field pickup** (temporary level, reverts at its TTL, refreshable on re-collect) **and** as a **permanent hold-full reward** that stays owned in a slot and auto-fires for the rest of the run on a level-derived interval — mirroring the Orbital Strike precedent.
- **D3 — Targeting.** It targets the **nearest live asteroid of any size tier**, computed with wrapped distance so an asteroid just across the screen seam (including one currently off-screen) is a valid target. It **never** targets non-asteroid enemies. It retargets immediately to the new nearest asteroid when its current target is destroyed. When no live asteroid exists it fires nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `mining_laser` power-up is present in `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) with a name, player-facing description, drop weight, temporary window and a level spec; it is a normal slot-occupying kind (not exempt at the six-slot cap) and has upgrade levels in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/data/powerup-levels.json`.
- Collecting a Mining Laser as a **field pickup** makes the ship auto-fire at the **nearest live asteroid** at a rapid beat-grid cadence for its temporary window; re-collecting refreshes the window and the level, and the level reverts to the permanent level (or unowned) when the window expires.
- Taking the **permanent hold-full reward** owns the Mining Laser in a slot and keeps it auto-firing at the nearest live asteroid for the rest of the run, on the level-derived cadence.
- Targeting uses **wrapped distance** so an asteroid across the screen seam (even off-screen) can be the nearest target; a nearer non-asteroid enemy is ignored in favour of an asteroid.
- The Mining Laser **never damages or targets non-asteroid enemies** (scouts, harvesters, boss, etc.).
- When no live asteroid exists, the Mining Laser fires **no shots** (no empty-space or forward-fallback fire).
- When the current target asteroid is destroyed, the Mining Laser retargets to the **new nearest** live asteroid on the next shot, including split children.
- The targeting rule is a pure, shared helper (asteroid-only nearest selection using wrapped distance) consumed by both the game and the gym, with gym↔game parity asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards.
- The Mining Laser is exercised in the appropriate gym scene (mineral/asteroid gym and/or the combat power-up gym) and shares the same core code as `PlayScene`.
- A code-drawn drop icon, catalogue description and HUD/active-effect readout exist, and the drop pool, hold-full choice and gym help surfaces include the new kind consistently.
- Unit tests cover: target selection (only asteroids, nearest with wrap seam, idle when none, retarget on kill/child spawn), cadence/fire path, temporary-window expiry and permanent ownership, and gym↔game parity.
- Documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 power-up table and count) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and any relevant wiki/docs entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can collect a Mining Laser that automatically chews through the nearest asteroids, making mineral farming passive so they can keep firing at enemies.

## Constraints

- Must not fork the power-up, effects, targeting, bullet or HUD seams — reuse the shared core so gym↔game parity holds by construction.
- Must not weaken the existing asteroid-skip rule for Arc/Orbital Strike (`src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`); the Mining Laser is the explicit, documented inverse.
- Must not target enemies, ever — even a nearer enemy must be ignored in favour of an asteroid.
- It is a slot-occupying power-up with upgrade levels, not a cannon-replacing weapon and not a timed hit-and-forget weapon drop.
- Tuning (fire cadence, damage, TTL, drop weight, level curve) is balance data recorded in the work item, not hard-coded behaviour spread across scenes.
- No frame-rate-dependent behaviour; cadence runs on the shared beat/onset grid.

## Existing state

- Power-ups are a 16-kind catalogue (`PowerUpId`) with a permanent/temporary level split, timed/instant windows, a shared `EffectsRegistry`, level specs in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` and data in `src/data/powerup-levels.json`; a run's loadout is capped at six permanent slots.
- Auto-firing power-ups already exist: the **Orbital Strike** (`strike`) fires a bolt at the nearest live **non-asteroid** enemy on a level-derived interval (`selectOrbitalStrikeTarget`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`); the **Mystery UFO** spawns a drone that seeks the nearest mineral.
- Auto-targeting eligibility is centralised in the pure `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (`isEligibleAutoTarget` / `isInertWorldHazard`), which *excludes* the `asteroid` archetype for Arc and Orbital Strike.
- Asteroids are `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` (archetype `'asteroid'`, 1 HP, three tiers, four-edge screen wrap). Small-asteroid mineral drops are resolved by `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` / `asteroidKillDrops.ts`.
- The shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `CombatScene.ts`) owns `_autoFire`, the beat clock and all power-up pulse/consumption steps; gym scenes inherit it.

## Desired change

Add a Mining Laser power-up kind whose auto-fire is an **asteroid-targeting** sibling of the Orbital Strike: a pure nearest-live-asteroid selector (wrapped distance, any tier), a shared core fire step that emits rapid laser shots at the target, permanent-slot and level-curve wiring, icon/HUD/drop wiring, and gym coverage — with the crystal-clear rule that it only ever fires at asteroids and is silent when none exist.

**Key Files:** (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `'mining_laser'` to `PowerUpId` and a `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry (name, description, drop weight, `temporaryWindow`, slot-occupying/consumable flags as appropriate).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/data/powerup-levels.json` — level spec (fire cadence, damage, temporary window, slot behaviour).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — per-run/pending state and the consume/resolve seam for the shared combat core.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared `_updateMiningLaser` step (target → fire on cadence), consuming the level store.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — resolve a fired shot against the asteroid through the shared damage path.
- New pure helper (e.g. `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` or an extension of `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`) — nearest-live-asteroid selector using wrapped distance.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` / `src/scenes/core/` bullet or hitscan seam — reuse the shared player-bullet path.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — default drop weight / drop-pool inclusion.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`, `src/powerups/dropDescriptions.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts` — icon, description, slot integration, readout.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` (and/or `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`) — gym coverage and parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — documentation.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts`, gym parity tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Target-selection edge cases.** Asteroids wrap at the screen seam; "nearest" must use wrapped distance (as `findNearestTarget` / `selectOrbitalStrikeTarget` do) so a target just across the seam — or off-screen across it — is chosen correctly.
- **Split chains.** Destroying a large/medium asteroid spawns children; the laser must retarget to a child (if still nearest) or another asteroid without firing into empty space.
- **Slot interaction.** It takes a permanent slot when owned and is not slot-cap-exempt; verify the hold-full choice gating and mini-boss wheel behave correctly at six owned slots.
- **Balance risk.** A rapidly auto-firing laser makes mineral farming near-passive; drop weight, cadence, damage and TTL should be tuned (start from Orbital Strike/Extra Life rarity precedents) and recorded.
- **Parity risk.** If any scene copies the fire logic instead of consuming the shared core, the duplicate-body guard/parity test will fail — implement once in the shared core.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Do **not** also add asteroid targeting to other weapons or add mining-laser variants; record such ideas as separate linked work items.

## Related work

- **Orbital Strike power-up (AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — nearest-target auto-firing power-up precedent (`strike`, `selectOrbitalStrikeTarget`, level-derived interval, field vs permanent).
- **Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69)** — the auto-target asteroid-skip rule the Mining Laser deliberately inverts.
- **Shared auto-target eligibility rule (AH-0MVVHAAUJ0080M9M / AH-0MVVHAD7Z005X5UW)** — `isEligibleAutoTarget` / `isInertWorldHazard`.
- **Asteroids drop collectable minerals (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q)** and the shared mineral kill-drop helper (AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB) — the mineral economy the laser feeds.
- **Gym minerals / asteroid gym** (`src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`) — natural observation scene.
- **Power-up catalogue + effects (epic AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z / AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — catalogue/level conventions.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery model.** Should the Mining Laser fire **alongside** the player's normal weapon (player can still shoot enemies), or is it acceptable for it to **replace** the main weapon while active? Options: (a) auxiliary/additive; (b) cannon-replacing. — **Recommended:** (a) auxiliary — a cannon-replacing weapon that can only hit asteroids would leave the player unable to damage enemies. **Answer (producer):** "It's a normal weapon power up that takes one of the slots available, with upgrade levels." → Resolved as an **additive, slot-occupying power-up with upgrade levels** (does not replace the cannon). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Acquisition & duration.** How should it be acquired? Options: (a) field pickup only, timed (~15 s) and refreshable; (b) field pickup **and** a permanent hold-full reward that repeats on a level-derived interval (Orbital Strike precedent); (c) permanent once collected. — **Recommended:** (b). **Answer (producer):** **B** — field pickup **and** permanent hold-full reward repeating on a level-derived interval. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — No-asteroid behaviour & asteroid tiers.** When no asteroid is present, should it be silent, and which asteroids are eligible? Options: (a) idle unless a live on-screen asteroid exists; target nearest any-tier asteroid; retarget on kill; (b) idle, but also consider off-screen asteroids across the wrap seam; (c) always fire forward when none exists. — **Recommended:** (a). **Answer (producer):** **B** — idle when none exists, but target the nearest live asteroid using **wrapped distance**, including asteroids across the screen seam / off-screen; nearest any-tier asteroid; retarget on kill. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08** – Remove the Power Pellet power-up from the game (completed)
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MVU3341U001B40T** – Orbital Strike must not target asteroids (producer rejection remediation) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muhmt5jc004wrsb, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvnsig1o0049g69, acceptance (+406 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, acceptance, active, actual, add (+387 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvnsig1o0049g69, acceptance, active, actual (+359 more)

## Plan (2026-11-09)

Decomposed into seven features, created in **test-first / dependency order**. Every phase is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs where the slice needs them), and each is a separate worktree/session.

| Phase | Feature | Depends on | Effort / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Mining-laser target rule (asteroid-only, wrapped) — AH-0MW9QMMOT0014IU0 | — | S / Low |
| F2 | Mining-laser catalogue kind and level curve — AH-0MW9QMNYP006ZO6T | — | S / Medium |
| F3 | Shared core mining-laser fire step — AH-0MW9QMP2P0032BWW | F1, F2 | M / High |
| F4 | Mining-laser beam VFX and audio cue — AH-0MW9QMQ7B005WFH9 | F3 | S / Low |
| F5 | Mining-laser surfaces: icon, description, drop, HUD — AH-0MW9QMRC7007HVHQ | F2 | S / Medium |
| F6 | Gym coverage and parity for the mining laser — AH-0MW9QMSI7005UU9P | F3, F5 | M / Medium |
| F7 | Docs: GDD §4.4, balancing, GYM_PARITY and guards — AH-0MW9QMTWL0075S32 | F5, F6 | XS / Low |

Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated with anything the previous phase learned (tuning values, helper names, VFX colour).

### Corrections to the predicted Key Files (facts, not intent)

- **`src/data/powerup-levels.json` does not exist.** The `src/data` parity JSONs are weapon-only (`weapon-levels.json`, `weapon-levels-parity.json`). Power-up level data lives solely in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, so the AC's "+ JSON" clause is satisfied by that module alone. No new JSON file is invented unless a separate parity-file capability is requested.
- **`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` is not the fire seam.** The laser resolves as an **instant beam** (see Recorded assumptions), so it reuses `CombatScene.damageEnemyViaAoe` (the shared kill seam) plus a new `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`, mirroring the `strike` precedent (`vfx/orbitalStrike.ts`). No change to the player-bullet path is needed.
- The targeting helper is `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` (the first, not the second, predicted option) and reuses `findNearestTarget` + `wrappedDistance` rather than re-implementing nearest selection.

### Recorded assumptions (correctable at review, not blocking)

1. **Instant beam, not a travelling projectile.** A projectile can collide with a non-asteroid enemy in flight, which the "never damages enemies" AC forbids; an instant resolve damages only the selected asteroid. A hitscan beam also works in gyms whose formation config collects no bullets (`GymMinerals` has `collectBullets: () => []`).
2. **No latched/banked shots.** Unlike the Orbital Strike (which latches a decided bolt so a pickup is never wasted), a cadence tick with no asteroid is simply skipped — silence is the required behaviour, and there is no single consumable to waste.
3. **Provisional balance values** (all catalogue/level data, retunable without code): cadence base **4 sixteenth-note steps = 750 ms**, −1 step per level, floor **1 step = 187.5 ms**; damage **1 → 2** whole hits (inert today — every asteroid tier is 1 HP); field TTL **10 s** (weapon-window precedent); drop weight **2** (Orbital Strike / Smart Bomb rarity).
4. **Slot behaviour:** a normal slot-counted kind — not `availableWhenSlotsFull`, not `fieldPickupOnly`, not `consumable`; rewarded when owned (level-up offer + mini-boss wedge).
5. **Gym coverage uses both observation scenes:** `GymMinerals` (asteroids only, currently no drop layer → opt in with a mining-laser-only spawner) shows the laser cutting, splitting and paying minerals; `GymPowerUpsCombat` (scouts only) shows the silence rule.
6. **The fire step lives in the shared core** and is called from `_tickPlayer` beside `_updateOrbitalStrike`, so `PlayScene` and every gym run identical code (the duplicate-body guard enforces it).

### OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking — defaults above are recorded so implementation can proceed)

- **Balance sign-off (game/balance designer).** Are the provisional cadence (0.75 s → 0.1875 s), damage (1 → 2), field TTL (10 s) and drop weight (2) the intended starting point, or should the laser be rarer/slower because passive farming is strong? The values are data; changing them later is a one-file edit in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/core/rules.ts`.
- **Feel (producer).** Instant beam vs travelling laser bolts. The instant beam is chosen for the "never damages enemies" guarantee and is the shipped default; a bolt look would need an asteroid-only collision filter and a parity test.
- **Damage axis.** Keep `miningLaserDamage` even though every asteroid is 1 HP today (catalogue-consistency), or drop the axis and make cadence the only level curve?

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (continued)

- **Q4 — Level-data location.** The AC names `src/data/powerup-levels.json`; no such file exists and the `src/data` parity files are weapon-only. **Answer (agent, from repository inspection):** level data lives in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` only; the AC is satisfied there and no JSON is invented. Evidence: `ls src/data` (no powerup file), `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`. Recorded as an AC-scope correction above.
- **Q5 — Fire delivery (beam vs projectile) for this codebase.** Auto-targeting offence's asteroid rule lives in `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (skip asteroids) and the strike's selector in `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`. **Answer (agent, research):** add the explicit inverse predicate + a sibling selector that reuses `findNearestTarget(..., world)`; resolve fire instantly through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, matching the `strike` VFX seam (`src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts`). Proposed to the producer as the non-blocking "feel" OPEN QUESTION above.
- **Q6 — Where can the behaviour be observed?** `GymMinerals` (`src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`) is asteroids-only but has **no** field-drop layer; `GymPowerUpsCombat` cycles power-ups but fields scouts only. **Answer (agent, research):** opt `GymMinerals` into the existing shared `powerUps` layer config with a mining-laser-only spawner, and add the kind to the combat gym's cycle — both consume the shared core, no gym fork. Recorded as F6.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-09 — Initial decomposition (F1–F7) created, dependency edges wired (F3←F1,F2; F4←F3; F5←F2; F6←F3,F5; F7←F5,F6), predicted-Key-Files corrections and recorded balance assumptions appended, three non-blocking open questions recorded.

# Add regression tests for pulse-wave lifecycle and constant-stroke render

## Problem

No automated tests cover the pulse-wave lifecycle: supersede, range exit, boss destroy, or constant-stroke render policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least one new or extended automated test covers the wave lifecycle (supersede, range exit, boss destroy) and the constant-stroke render path.
- Supersede test: fire two volleys inside one wave lifetime; assert exactly one wave sprite in the display list.
- Range exit test: let a wave reach the edge of the screen; assert zero wave sprites in the display list.
- Boss destroy test: destroy the boss; assert zero wave sprites remain.
- Constant-stroke test: assert that the wave Graphics object uses a constant line width regardless of radius.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files

- src/entities/Boss.test.ts — new or extended tests for wave lifecycle.

## Context

Parent: **Mining laser** (AH-0MW81181P007BDRU). Producer decisions D1–D3 are recorded there: auxiliary slot-occupying power-up with levels; field pickup + permanent hold-full reward; asteroid-only nearest targeting with wrapped distance.

This is the **test-first foundation slice**: the pure, shared targeting rule the rest of the feature consumes. Nothing here boots a Phaser scene.

Existing seams to reuse (do **not** fork):

- `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` — `INERT_WORLD_HAZARD_ARCHETYPES` / `isInertWorldHazard` (the asteroid-skip rule for Arc/Orbital Strike). The Mining Laser is the **documented inverse** of that rule: it targets **only** the inert hazard archetype. Do not weaken or invert the existing predicate; add a separate, explicitly-named predicate next to it.
- `src/utils/aoe.ts` — `findNearestTarget(originX, originY, targets, exclude, accepts, world)` already supports an `accepts` predicate **and** a `WrapWorld` for wrapped distance.
- `src/utils/wrapGeometry.ts` — `wrappedDistance(origin, point, world)`; `src/core/constants.ts` — `GAME_WIDTH` / `GAME_HEIGHT` for the world.

## Goal / user story

As a player, my Mining Laser always fires at the nearest live rock **anywhere on the wrapped playfield**, never at empty space and never at a nearer enemy — so farming minerals never diverts my aim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new module `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` exports an asteroid-only predicate and `selectMiningLaserTarget(origin, entities, world?)`; both are pure (no Phaser, no scene imports) and unit-testable without booting a scene.
- Selection returns the **nearest live asteroid of any size tier** using **wrapped distance** (an asteroid just across a screen seam, including one currently off-screen across it, can be the nearest target).
- A **nearer non-asteroid enemy** (scout, harvester, boss, `lane-traffic`, an entity with no archetype) is never selected; only `archetype === 'asteroid'` bodies are eligible.
- Dead asteroids (`alive === false`) are never selected; when no live asteroid exists the helper returns `null` — the caller's cue to fire nothing.
- Re-running selection after the previous target dies returns the new nearest live asteroid, including a freshly spawned split child.
- Unit tests in `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.test.ts` cover: only-asteroids, nearest selection, seam wrap (both axes), off-screen-across-seam, nearer-enemy-ignored, all-dead → `null`, empty field → `null`, retarget after kill and after split children join the field.
- `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` gains the inverse predicate with a doc comment naming the Mining Laser and the parent item id; `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts` gains a case pinning that the two rules are exact inverses for the asteroid archetype and that `isEligibleAutoTarget` behaviour for Arc/Strike is unchanged.


### Parent-AC coverage

Restated verbatim from the parent (**Mining laser**, AH-0MW81181P007BDRU). These are satisfied **collectively** by this item together with its sibling phases; this item must not regress them.

- Targeting uses **wrapped distance** so an asteroid across the screen seam (even off-screen) can be the nearest target; a nearer non-asteroid enemy is ignored in favour of an asteroid.
- The Mining Laser **never damages or targets non-asteroid enemies** (scouts, harvesters, boss, etc.).
- When the current target asteroid is destroyed, the Mining Laser retargets to the **new nearest** live asteroid on the next shot, including split children.
- The targeting rule is a pure, shared helper (asteroid-only nearest selection using wrapped distance) consumed by both the game and the gym, with gym↔game parity asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards.
- Unit tests cover: target selection (only asteroids, nearest with wrap seam, idle when none, retarget on kill/child spawn), cadence/fire path, temporary-window expiry and permanent ownership, and gym↔game parity.

## Implementation notes / Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` (new), `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.test.ts` (new).
- `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` + `.test.ts` — inverse predicate (e.g. `isMinedWorldHazard` / `MINED_HAZARD_ARCHETYPES`); keep `INERT_WORLD_HAZARD_ARCHETYPES` untouched.
- Follow the `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts` shape (interface with optional `archetype`, thin delegation to shared helpers, long doc comment naming the parent item) so the pair reads as siblings.

## Deliverables

- Pure helper + its unit tests + eligibility inverse predicate and its test.
- A short note in the parent work item recording the final helper/predicate names.

data.description:
## Context

Parent: **Mining laser** (AH-0MW81181P007BDRU). Decisions D1/D2: normal slot-occupying power-up **with upgrade levels**; field pickup (temporary level + TTL window, refreshable) **and** permanent hold-full reward that keeps auto-firing for the run — the Orbital Strike precedent (`strike`).

This slice adds the kind and its data/state only: catalogue entry, level curve, and the registry cadence state that the shared core will drive in the next slice.

**Note on the parent AC wording:** the parent AC names `src/data/powerup-levels.json`; **no such file exists** (the `src/data` parity JSONs are weapon-only: `weapon-levels.json`, `weapon-levels-parity.json`). Level data lives solely in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`. Do not invent a new JSON file; if a parity JSON is genuinely wanted, raise it as a separate item.

## Goal / user story

As a balance designer, the Mining Laser's fire cadence, damage, TTL and rarity are catalogue/level data I can retune without touching scene code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `'mining_laser'` is added to `PowerUpId` and `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` in `src/powerups/types.ts` with `name`, player-facing `description`, `duration`, `temporaryWindow: 10`, and **no** `availableWhenSlotsFull` (it is a normal slot-occupying kind, gated at the six-slot cap) and no `consumable`/`singleUse`/`fieldPickupOnly` flags.
- `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.mining_laser` in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` declares the two cadence/power axes with rationale comments, and the id is appended to `POWER_UP_LEVEL_IDS`.
- Proposed defaults (recorded as balance data, tunable without code change):
  - `miningLaserInterval` — seconds between laser shots, expressed as whole **16th-note steps of the shared beat lattice** (one beat = 4 steps = 750 ms at 80 BPM): base **4 steps = 750 ms** (one beat), shortening by 1 step per level, floored at **1 step = 187.5 ms**; curve `linear-clamped`, `discrete: false`. Named beat/step constants live in `src/core/constants.ts` alongside `STRIKE_INTERVAL_BEATS_*`.
  - `miningLaserDamage` — whole hits, `exponential-saturation` base 1, cap 2, `discrete: true`; rationale must state that every asteroid tier is 1 HP today, so the axis exists for catalogue consistency and future armoured rocks.

## Context

Parent: **Mining laser** (AH-0MW81181P007BDRU). This is the **shared gameplay core** slice: the one fire step the game and every gym inherit, so gym↔game parity holds by construction (AGENTS.md § Game Architecture Conventions / AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).

Depends on F1 (pure asteroid-only wrapped selector) and F2 (catalogue kind + `EffectsRegistry` cadence state).

Design decision (recorded assumption): the laser resolves as an **instant beam to the selected target**, not a travelling projectile. Rationale: a travelling bullet could collide with a non-asteroid enemy in flight, which the parent AC forbids outright; an instant resolve applies damage only to the selected asteroid. Damage routes through the existing shared kill seam `CombatScene.damageEnemyViaAoe` (takeDamage → finaliseEnemyKill), so score/drop/wave accounting and mineral drops run exactly once, unchanged.

## Goal / user story

As a player, whenever a Mining Laser is active my ship automatically fires a rapid laser at the nearest asteroid, and nothing at all when there is no asteroid — the same code in the game and in every gym.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `CombatCoreScene` gains `_updateMiningLaser(dt)` driven from `_tickPlayer` (placed alongside `_updateOrbitalStrike`), which asks the registry whether a shot is due and delegates resolution to a single overridable hook `onMiningLaserFire(target)`; the hook's default does nothing, so a scene that owns no asteroid seam stays silent.
- `CombatScene` overrides the hook: it resolves one laser shot at the nearest live asteroid from `selectMiningLaserTarget` over `getEnemyEntities()` (asteroids in `PlayScene` are pushed into `spawned`, confirmed), applies the level-resolved damage through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, and spawns the beam VFX/cue (F4 provides the module; a temporary no-op is acceptable only if F4 lands after this item — record it).
- The step **never** damages or targets a non-asteroid enemy: no scout, harvester, boss, hazard or `lane-traffic` body is ever selected; a nearer enemy is ignored (parent AC).
- With no live asteroid on the field the step emits **no shots at all** — no forward fallback, no empty-space fire, no latched/banked shots.
- Destroying the current target retargets on the **next shot** to the new nearest live asteroid, including a split child, with no wasted shot (a shot is only emitted when a target exists).
- Cadence is frame-rate independent: the same elapsed time produces the same number of shots regardless of `dt` stepping, and every shot lands on the shared beat lattice.
- Tests (write first) in `src/scenes/core/miningLaserFire.test.ts` (new) and/or `CombatScene.test.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.test.ts` cover: only-asteroid damage; nearer-enemy ignored; silence with no asteroid; retarget after a kill and after a split child spawns; cadence measured end-to-end through the real shared step (mirroring `src/scenes/core/orbitalStrikeRetention.test.ts`); damage resolved once per shot (kill accounting not double-counted).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` passes unchanged (no duplicated body is reintroduced by the new code).


### Parent-AC coverage

Restated verbatim from the parent (**Mining laser**, AH-0MW81181P007BDRU). These are satisfied **collectively** by this item together with its sibling phases; this item must not regress them.

- Collecting a Mining Laser as a **field pickup** makes the ship auto-fire at the **nearest live asteroid** at a rapid beat-grid cadence for its temporary window; re-collecting refreshes the window and the level, and the level reverts to the permanent level (or unowned) when the window expires.
- Taking the **permanent hold-full reward** owns the Mining Laser in a slot and keeps it auto-firing at the nearest live asteroid for the rest of the run, on the level-derived cadence.
- The Mining Laser **never damages or targets non-asteroid enemies** (scouts, harvesters, boss, etc.).
- When no live asteroid exists, the Mining Laser fires **no shots** (no empty-space or forward-fallback fire).
- Unit tests cover: target selection (only asteroids, nearest with wrap seam, idle when none, retarget on kill/child spawn), cadence/fire path, temporary-window expiry and permanent ownership, and gym↔game parity.

## Implementation notes / Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (`_updateMiningLaser`, `onMiningLaserFire`, `_tickPlayer` call site + doc comments naming the parent id).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`onMiningLaserFire` override).
- `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` (from F1), `src/powerups/effects.ts` (from F2).
- Tests: `src/scenes/core/miningLaserFire.test.ts` (new), `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`.

## Dependencies

F1 (target rule), F2 (kind + registry cadence).

## Deliverables

- Shared core step + hook + game-path resolution, with tests; the design assumption (instant beam, not projectile) recorded on the parent.

## Context

Parent: **Mining laser** (AH-0MW81181P007BDRU). Precedent: `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts` — a self-contained VFX module that owns its look, its timing **and** its audio cue, so no call site can forget the sound and no scene can fork it (AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V).

Depends on F3 (the fire step/hook exists). The Mining Laser fires **rapidly** (up to once per 16th note), so the visual must be cheap and must never wash the screen: a thin beam drawn ship→target for a very short life, no persistent layer churn.

## Goal / user story

As a player, I can see and hear the Mining Laser working — a crisp laser tick between my ship and the rock it is cutting — without it competing with enemy-fire telegraphs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts` exports `spawnMiningLaserBeam(scene, from, to, options)` that draws a thin, code-drawn beam (Phaser Graphics or a shared bullet-shape seam — no new assets, no textures, no runtime dependencies) between the ship and the target, lasting a short fixed duration and destroying itself; repeated shots at the same target must not leak game objects or grow the display list unbounded.
- The module owns its dedicated audio cue (a short laser tick added to `src/audio/effects.ts` and registered in the cue manifest), played from the VFX module so no call site can forget it and so the cue stays rate-limited to the shot cadence.
- The beam is drawn from the player's current position to the **current target's** position, using wrapped-aware aim so a target across the screen seam reads correctly (the beam must not draw across the whole screen when the target is just past the seam — render it as the short through-the-edge segment, reusing the wrapped-ray geometry helper if one fits: `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` `traceWrappedRay`).
- Visuals are wired from the shared seam only (`CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire`), so `PlayScene` and every gym show the identical beam and cue.
- Tests: `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.test.ts` covers beam creation/duration/cleanup, wrapped aim across each seam, and cue invocation; `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` and the audio effects contract test cover the new cue; a VFX docs guard (mirroring `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.docs.test.ts`) is added only if the GDD documents the beam.
- No frame-rate-dependent lifetime: the beam lifetime is a delta-driven timer, not a tick count.


### Parent-AC coverage

Restated verbatim from the parent (**Mining laser**, AH-0MW81181P007BDRU). These are satisfied **collectively** by this item together with its sibling phases; this item must not regress them.

- Collecting a Mining Laser as a **field pickup** makes the ship auto-fire at the **nearest live asteroid** at a rapid beat-grid cadence for its temporary window; re-collecting refreshes the window and the level, and the level reverts to the permanent level (or unowned) when the window expires.

## Implementation notes / Key Files

- `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts` (new) + `.test.ts` (new), plus optional `.docs.test.ts`.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` (cue), `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` (`traceWrappedRay`) reused for through-seam geometry.
